macro.regime: Cautiously risk-on but fragile: NVDA beat-and-raise offsets a hot-but-in-line PCE, with Warsh's Jackson Hole debut the last binary catalyst before September FOMC
macro.narrative: Wednesday 26 Aug's complete US close: S&P 500 +0.3% to ~7,676-7,677, Nasdaq +0.7-0.8% to ~26,130-26,151, VIX -1.55% to 15.21 -- calm into a stacked data day. Core PCE m/m printed in line at 0.2% (y/y 3.3%, still well above target -- 'elevated but stable,' not accelerating); Prelim GDP q/q held at 1.5%, confirming the deceleration from Q1's 2.1% without a recession signal. After the close, Nvidia crushed FQ2: revenue $96.2B (+106% y/y), EPS $2.22, FQ3 guidance $108B vs $104.2B consensus, shares +14.5% after-hours, AWS separately announcing a 2-million-GPU order on Nvidia's new Vera CPU -- futures firmed into Thursday's Asia open on the print. Gold/silver ETFs and miners pulled back (GLD -1.58%, SLV -1.17%, GDX -2.94%) even as futures held firm (GC=F +0.50%, SI=F +0.14%), a timing/ETF-vs-future divergence coinciding with the hot-but-in-line inflation print tempering near-term cut hopes; silver still capped its best month in years (~+17-18% in August). Oil extended its slide (Brent -2.24%, WTI -0.59%) on continuing Iran-Oman Strait-of-Hormuz de-escalation talks. The dominant near-term catalyst is now Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote as Chair, Friday 28 Aug -- he has explicitly declined forward guidance and left a 2026 hike on the table since the July FOMC hold at 3.50-3.75%, even as September hike odds have eased to ~30% on a weak July jobs report. Net: a genuinely constructive tape (AI capex intact, inflation not re-accelerating, calm VIX, tight-but-not-complacent credit spreads) capped by real uncertainty over a hawkish-surprise Fed chair's Friday speech and a historic long-bond selloff (30Y >5.3%, TLT at a 22-year low) reflecting fiscal/duration stress independent of the Fed.
